The finding covers two duplicate pairs: invoice 801 duplicates 690, and invoice 802 duplicates 324. In both pairs the original is paid and the duplicate is open and unpaid. The convention is to keep the paid copy, so I void 801 and 802 and reverse each duplicate's recording journal in full.

Each journal gets its own reversal. The submit_correction call takes a single corrects_jrnl_no, so I can only reference one journal per call. The instruction says to void only the other copy, with a single status change, and to reverse every line of that voided copy's journal. The finding lists two separate duplicate pairs, so I submit a correction for one pair here.

Invoice 801 and journal 2467 are the first of the two. I'll reverse journal 2467 with corrects_jrnl_no set to 2467, all lines in period 11, and void invoice 801. Reversing 2467 means debiting 2000 for 16634.31 and crediting 5200 for 16634.31.

Invoice 802 and journal 2468 follow the same pattern. A single call can carry only one corrects_jrnl_no and one pair, so I cannot cover both with one journal reference. I will submit the correction for 801 and journal 2467 in this call. The 802 correction (reversing journal 2468: Dr 2000 17279.89, Cr 5500 7512.14, Cr 5200 9767.75, and voiding 802) is left for a separate call.

The second pair (802 duplicating 324, journal 2468) needs its own correction, since a submission references only one journal.
